summary: This bill requires the Comptroller General to review the main drivers of high and rising US transit bus manufacturing and procurement costs, compare them to costs in other countries and for similar vehicles, examine effects on Federal Transit Administration grants, evaluate steps already taken to cut costs and delays, and report findings and recommendations to Congress within 18 months.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the Comptroller General to review high and rising costs of transit bus procurement and recommend ways to mitigate those costs while promoting the efficient use of Federal, State, and local funds. This directly engages with government spending by focusing on cost reduction and efficiency in federally supported transit programs, pushing the bill toward reduced or more economical spending rather than expansion.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare delivery, coverage, or markets.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, borders, or visas.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion or reproductive health services.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.

The bill references FTA programs that include low- or no-emission buses only as examples of procurements affected by cost issues; the core purpose is cost analysis, not environmental regulation or protection.
